notes:
Summary: Arbor Encore is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for productionizing an LLM-powered fraud-detection chat assistant plus embeddings for transaction similarity. Primary emphasis is on cryptographic controls and auditability. CTO quote: "Keys must remain under our tenancy; any automatic key export is a non-starter."

Encryption posture discussed on 2026-02-14 call:
- In-transit: customer requires TLS 1.3 + mutual TLS (mTLS) for all service-to-service connections inside the VPC and between Redwood's private agents and customer-side proxies. Must support client cert rotation and short-lived certs (<= 24h recommended).
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM for model cache, KV caches, and logs. All persistent storage encrypted and bound to envelope keys.
- KMS integration: mandatory customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS (preferred) or Azure Key Vault. HSM-backed keys required for primary envelope keys. Support for external HSM (CloudHSM) and BYOK workflows discussed.
- Key rotation: support for automated rotation every 90 days for envelope keys and immediate rotation on suspected compromise. Redwood must support rekeying without downtime and provide a replayable migration plan for cached KV material.
- Secrets management: integration with HashiCorp Vault or cloud-native Secrets Manager. Requirement: secrets never persist in plaintext on disk; retrieval uses short-lived tokens and signed AWS STS assume-role flows.
- Audit logging: all key usage must be audited with entry-level logs shipped to customer Splunk/Datadog/S3 bucket. Audit logs must include key id, operation, caller identity, timestamp, and request context. Retention control: 7 years for high-risk events; configurable per-bucket.
- Network constraints: VPC-only endpoints, no public IPs on inference agents, mandatory VPC peering or PrivateLink; egress to internet must be blocked except for approved endpoints.
